AUTHOR: D. Morales; N. Pérez-Pérez; D. S. Benítez; M. Herrera; O. Camacho; A. Hearn
TITLE: Monitoring Tunas and Sharks Using YOLO Models in the Galápagos Islands
SPECIES: Silky shark (Carcharhinus falciformis), tiger shark (Galeocerdo cuvier), tuna
DATA: Own underwater video clips from Galápagos (two 1-min training clips; 10-s and 15-s test clips)
D2: 90/10 of 229 frames from two 1-min clips, 5-fold CV on training portion; separate 10-s and 15-s clips for count test
D_EV: Sec. II.E: 'To ensure a robust evaluation and prevent data contamination, no frames from the test videos were included'; '90% of the 229 annotated images were used for training'
R_EV: Sec. II.F: 'Two distinct sets of videos (10-second and 15-second clips), not used in training, were reserved for testing' (same Galápagos footage source)
C_EV: Table III: 'False Positives / Overcounts ... Yes (Overcount) ... Yes (False Positives)' per model; no confidence threshold value reported
E_EV: Table III: 'Per-video detection counts... Expected ... Tuna >20 ... Tiger Shark 1 ... Silky Shark 2' compared with each model's counts
METR: mAP@50, mAP@50-95, per-video counts, inference time, FP/overcount flag
NOTE: Headline mAP (Table II) comes from a 90/10 frame split of frames from the same two training clips (coded 이미지/프레임 무작위; D4 = Y because contamination is explicitly discussed, though the description is internally inconsistent). Separate unseen test clips used only for count comparison. Camera platform not stated. C5: false positives/overcounts flagged per model (yes/no) on test clips, no rate; coded as duplicate-count handling (could be '둘 다'); no confidence threshold value given despite PR-based threshold discussion -> C_ALL P. 'Expected' counts presumably from human viewing of the same clips.
